Set up for later: a second Performance on the MODX for the [full scores](../theory/analysed-scores/full-scores.qmd), one Part per
section of the orchestra, so a score can play on the board's orchestral voices instead of the site's samples. The full-score player
does not send to the MODX yet; this page is the plan for its sixteen Parts and lets you try each voice on the board now.

## Make the Performance

1. Start from an empty Performance (or any one, then replace its Parts) and give each Part below its voice: touch the Part,
   then **[CATEGORY SEARCH]** and the category shown (Strings, Woodwind, Brass, Chromatic Perc, Drum/Perc) to find the name.
2. **Part n plays on channel n**: with Utility → Settings → MIDI → *MIDI I/O Mode* = **Multi**, each channel reaches only its Part.
3. Arpeggios and motion sequences off on every Part; Keyboard Control off on all but the one you want to play from the keys.
4. A hall reverb for the whole Performance; each Part's reverb send a little higher for the strings than for the brass.
5. Store it as a User Performance named **Site Orchestra**, separate from the Site Band one.

The names below come from Yamaha's MODX+ Data List, read through its PDF text, where the table's columns run together: check
the spelling on the board. Bold is the first to try. Write what you choose in the last column; it is kept in this browser.

## Connect

```{=html}
<div class="mo-row">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-primary" id="mo-connect">Connect the MODX</button>
  <span id="mo-status" class="mo-note">Not connected</span>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="mo-all">▶ Every Part in turn</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="mo-stop">■ Stop</button>
</div>
<p class="mo-note">▶ plays a short broken chord in the middle of that instrument's range on its channel (a few hits on the
percussion Part), so you can hear the voice you loaded. Load the Site Orchestra Performance first.</p>
```

## The sixteen Parts

```{=html}
<table class="mo-table" id="mo-parts"></table>
<p class="mo-note">Staff names: which full-score staves go to the Part (the full-score player names its instruments in
Italian, English or German). A score with more staves than this (two flutes and a piccolo, four horns) shares a Part within the
family; the "also" line says which voice to use if a doubling instrument has its own staff.</p>
```

## Still to do

- The full-score player sends each staff to its Part (as the band does through `modx.js`), with a Site / MODX switch.
- Pizzicato, tremolo and mutes: a score marks them and the player does not play them yet. On the MODX they need another voice
  (Pizzicato Strings, Tremolo Strings) or a Scene on the string Parts; no Parts are left in sixteen, so a Scene switch is the likely way.
- Dynamics: the player shapes velocity from the written dynamics ("Even out the loudness"); the MODX string and brass voices
  change colour with velocity, so they may need the velocity range set per Part, as the band's instruments have on the MODX page.

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var O = window.ModxOrchestra, M = window.BandModx, $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); }, LS = "modx-orchestra";
  var mine = {}; try { mine = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LS) || "{}") || {}; } catch (e) {}
  var CAT = { Flutes: "Woodwind", Oboes: "Woodwind", Clarinets: "Woodwind", Bassoons: "Woodwind", Horns: "Brass", Trumpets: "Brass", Trombones: "Brass",
    Tuba: "Brass", Timpani: "Drum/Perc", Percussion: "Drum/Perc", "Harp, keyboards": "Chromatic Perc / Keyboard" };
  function esc(s) { return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) { return { "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" }[c]; }); }
  $("mo-parts").innerHTML = "<tr><th>Part</th><th>Voices to try</th><th class='mo-hide'>Staff names</th><th></th><th>Your choice</th></tr>" + O.PARTS.map(function (p) {
    return "<tr><td><b>" + p.ch + "</b> " + esc(p.part) + "<div class='mo-also'>" + esc(CAT[p.part] || "Strings") + "</div></td>" +
      "<td><ol class='mo-pick'>" + p.pick.map(function (n) { return "<li>" + esc(n) + "</li>"; }).join("") + "</ol>" +
      (p.also ? "<div class='mo-also'>Also: " + p.also.map(esc).join("; ") + "</div>" : "") + (p.note ? "<div class='mo-also'>" + esc(p.note) + "</div>" : "") + "</td>" +
      "<td class='mo-hide mo-also'>" + esc(p.staves) + "</td>" +
      "<td><button type='button' class='btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary' data-ch='" + p.ch + "'>▶</button></td>" +
      "<td><input type='text' data-c='" + p.ch + "' value='" + esc(mine[p.ch] || "") + "' placeholder='" + esc(p.pick[0]) + "'></td></tr>";
  }).join("");
  $("mo-parts").oninput = function (e) { var c = e.target.dataset.c; if (!c) return; mine[c] = e.target.value; try { localStorage.setItem(LS, JSON.stringify(mine)); } catch (x) {} };
  var timers = [];
  function stop() { timers.forEach(clearTimeout); timers = []; if (M) M.stop(); }
  function play(p, at0) {
    var beat = 600; O.phrase(p).forEach(function (n) { M.note(p.ch, n.midi, n.vel, at0 + n.at * beat, n.dur * beat); });
    return at0 + 5 * beat;
  }
  function ready() { if (!M || !M.connected()) { $("mo-status").textContent = "Connect the MODX first."; return false; } return true; }
  $("mo-parts").onclick = function (e) { var c = e.target.dataset && e.target.dataset.ch; if (!c || !ready()) return; stop(); play(O.PARTS[c - 1], performance.now() + 100); };
  $("mo-all").onclick = function () { if (!ready()) return; stop(); var t = performance.now() + 100;
    O.PARTS.forEach(function (p) { (function (p, at) { timers.push(setTimeout(function () { $("mo-status").textContent = "Playing: " + p.ch + " " + p.part; }, Math.max(0, at - performance.now()))); })(p, t); t = play(p, t); }); };
  $("mo-stop").onclick = stop;
  $("mo-connect").onclick = function () { M.connect().then(function (n) { $("mo-status").textContent = "Connected: " + n; }, function (e) { $("mo-status").textContent = e.message; }); };
  if (M && M.connected()) $("mo-status").textContent = "Connected: " + M.portName();
})();
</script>
```
